<issue identifier="ABA-143">
<title>CAGR glidepath Y1 anchor blows out Y-axis when fcf_ttm is negative (AMZN)</title>
<description>
**Surfaced by:** <issue id="b2f52e69-f10f-4caa-951c-d0c021ad5837">ABA-138</issue> verification on AMZN, 2026-05-19.

## Problem

`CagrGlidepath.jsx` back-derives the Year 1 implicit Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) as:

```
y1_cagr = (scenarios[s].y1_fcf / stages.model.fcf_ttm) − 1
```

AMZN's `fcf_ttm` is **−$11.77B** (capex spike, not a structural problem — this is exactly why the model maintains `fcf_normalized` alongside the raw TTM). When the denominator is negative and the numerator is positive, the resulting "growth rate" is mathematically nonsensical (Y1 lands at roughly **−700% / −800% / −900%** for bear / base / bull).

This stretches the chart's Y-axis from **\~−864% to +238%**, compressing the Y2–Y5 detail (where the real signal lives — the capped 18–24% growth band) into an illegible strip near zero. See attached screenshot in the original conversation.

All four acceptance criteria for <issue id="b2f52e69-f10f-4caa-951c-d0c021ad5837">ABA-138</issue> still pass mechanically (monotone ordering, cap callout, pre-profit guard, three colour-coded lines) — but the chart fails its actual purpose of *communicating the glidepath* on AMZN.

## Proposed fix

When `stages.model.fcf_ttm <= 0`, substitute `stages.model.fcf_normalized` (or equivalent smoothed value already in the report) as the Year 1 anchor denominator. The base-case Y1 CAGR for AMZN would then derive from a sensible positive base, putting Y1 in the same band as Y2–Y5 and letting the cap-callout story dominate the visual.

## Acceptance criteria

* For AMZN: chart Y-axis range fits within ±50% (or whatever range Y2–Y5 naturally occupy + reasonable headroom).
* Year 2–Year 5 detail is visually readable (line bends at the cap are visible without zooming).
* META, NVDA (if <issue id="5decc161-2ee1-4551-b235-bad803c5817d">ABA-142</issue> re-classifies it), and other ESTABLISHED tickers with positive `fcf_ttm` render unchanged.
* Pre-profit guard still fires.
* Cap callout still fires when `growth_rate.cap_applied === true`.

## Verification

`npm run dev` → Model tab → AMZN. Y2–Y5 detail readable, Y1 anchor in same order of magnitude as Y2–Y5 points.
</description>

<title>/stock:model report — glidepath + scenario fan visuals</title>
<description>
## Problem

After <issue id="89e1f4f4-8b04-4c5b-9931-7f4f837de45f">ABA-110</issue> (SBC (Stock-Based Compensation) strip) and <issue id="e78e36cd-49f1-441f-96a9-317acc594230">ABA-111</issue> (growth-rate cap) landed, `/stock:model` now produces honest but **stark-looking** scenario outputs. Example META 2026-05-17:

* Bear IV (Intrinsic Value): $184
* Base IV: $393
* Bull IV: $778
* Current price: $614

Reading the base case in isolation ("$393 vs $614 → 36% overvalued") is misleading without the trajectory context. The base case mechanically applies the consensus growth ceiling in Y2 (META: 52% trailing → 18% capped), which looks like a cliff but is a smoothing artifact of the spec. A reader anchored on "base = realistic central case" will misread it as "the model thinks META is 36% overvalued" when the actual message is "the market is pricing META as a bull case — here's what has to keep going right."

## Why now

Thesis construction depends on **explaining how the numbers got where they got** — more than the numbers themselves. Without visuals, the reader has to do the unpacking in their head; with visuals, the trajectory and the asymmetry are immediately legible.

User quote (2026-05-17 session): *"reading a 'base case' that's so far from the current stock price has some context — it's unlikely that a company that has kept massive momentum in growth will suddenly stop, so this is important to put into context."*

## Scope

Add three visuals to the report UI for ESTABLISHED-path Model output:

1. **CAGR (Compound Annual Growth Rate) glidepath** — line chart showing trailing-3y CAGR (clean, SBC-stripped), then Y1→Y5 projected CAGR for each scenario (bear/base/bull). Annotate cap point ("capped from 52.1% by 18% fallback ceiling" for the base line).
2. **FCF (Free Cash Flow) margin trajectory** — area chart showing 3y historical reported vs clean FCF margin, with a constant-margin extension for Y1→Y5. Visually surfaces that base case assumes flat-line margins (no operating leverage) — and invites the user to consider whether they buy that assumption.
3. **Scenario fan chart** — cone/fan plot of Y1→Y5 FCF projection for bear/base/bull, with the corresponding terminal-year discounted-to-PV (Present Value) markers, and the current price line for reference.

## Acceptance criteria

1. UI renders the three visuals for any covered ticker's latest `reports/TICKER_YYYYMMDD.json` where `stages.model` is present.
2. Cap-point annotation reads from `stages.model.growth_rate` block (added in <issue id="e78e36cd-49f1-441f-96a9-317acc594230">ABA-111</issue>) — specifically `trailing_3y_cagr`, `applied_base_cagr`, `cap_source`.
3. FCF margin chart reads clean and reported series from `stages.model.fcf_margin_ttm` (clean) and `stages.model.fcf_margin_ttm_reported` (reported, added in <issue id="89e1f4f4-8b04-4c5b-9931-7f4f837de45f">ABA-110</issue>).
4. Scenario fan chart sources from `stages.model.scenarios.{bear,base,bull}` (existing).
5. Each visual has a one-sentence caption explaining the assumption it surfaces (not the chart mechanics — the *thesis* implication).
6. Pre-profit variant either gets its own analogous visuals or is explicitly scoped out (decide during design).

## Out of scope

* Glidepath shaping (introducing year-by-year CAGR taper instead of flat Y2-Y5) — separate ticket if worth doing
* Adding a margin-expansion lever to *base* case — separate methodology ticket if worth doing
* Sensitivity heatmap (WACC × g) — separate ticket

## Related

* Builds on <issue id="89e1f4f4-8b04-4c5b-9931-7f4f837de45f">ABA-110</issue> (SBC strip surfaces clean vs reported margins in JSON)
* Builds on <issue id="e78e36cd-49f1-441f-96a9-317acc594230">ABA-111</issue> (growth-rate block surfaces cap mechanics in JSON)
* Likely lives in Wave 4 (UI/report polish) of M5; defer until playbook layer (<issue id="70664e55-f843-4fed-8462-d8e6e78141cb">ABA-112</issue>) lands so visuals reference playbook narrative

## Methodology footnote (for the reader)

The base case is intentionally a **"stop overdelivering"** anchor:

* Margins flat at today's clean FCF margin (no operating-leverage assumption)
* Growth decelerates from trailing print to consensus-5y ceiling (or 18% fallback) in Y2
* Discount rate at WACC (Weighted Average Cost of Capital) baseline

The bull case is where margin-expansion + sustained-growth assumptions live. This is by design — it forces the thesis to articulate which levers it's betting on, rather than baking optimism into the central case.

22	  if (value == null || Number.isNaN(value)) return '—';

26	function capFootnote(growthRate) {

35	export default function CagrGlidepath({ model }) {
36	  if (!model) return null;
37	  const method = typeof model.method === 'string' ? model.method : '';
38	  if (method.startsWith('pre-profit')) return null;
39	
40	  const fcfTtm = model.fcf_ttm;
41	  const scenarios = model.scenarios ?? {};
42	  const growthRate = model.growth_rate ?? {};
43	  const trailing = growthRate.trailing_3y_cagr;
44	  const hasTrailing = trailing != null && Number.isFinite(trailing);
45	
46	  // Build series: [trailing?, y1, y2, y3, y4, y5] per scenario. Drop the
47	  // trailing column entirely when growth_rate.trailing_3y_cagr is missing
48	  // (older pre-v1.11 reports), so we never plot NaN.
49	  const series = SCENARIOS.map(({ key, label, color }) => {
50	    const s = scenarios[key];
51	    if (!s || fcfTtm == null || !Number.isFinite(fcfTtm) || fcfTtm === 0) {
52	      return null;
53	    }
54	    if (!Number.isFinite(s.y1_fcf) || !Number.isFinite(s.y2_5_cagr)) {
55	      return null;
56	    }
57	    const y1Cagr = s.y1_fcf / fcfTtm - 1;
58	    const y25Cagr = s.y2_5_cagr;
59	    const points = hasTrailing
60	      ? [trailing, y1Cagr, y25Cagr, y25Cagr, y25Cagr, y25Cagr]
61	      : [y1Cagr, y25Cagr, y25Cagr, y25Cagr, y25Cagr];
62	    return { key, label, color, points };
63	  }).filter(Boolean);
64	
65	  if (series.length === 0) return null;
66	
67	  const xLabels = hasTrailing ? X_LABELS : X_LABELS.slice(1);
68	
69	  // Y-axis domain: include trailing + all scenario points, pad 10%
70	  const allValues = series.flatMap((s) => s.points).filter((v) => v != null && Number.isFinite(v));
71	  if (allValues.length === 0) return null;
72	
73	  let yMin = Math.min(0, ...allValues);
74	  let yMax = Math.max(...allValues);
75	  if (yMin === yMax) yMax = yMin + 0.1;
76	  const yPad = (yMax - yMin) * 0.1;
77	  yMin -= yPad;
78	  yMax += yPad;
79	
80	  const plotW = WIDTH - PAD_LEFT - PAD_RIGHT;
81	  const plotH = HEIGHT - PAD_TOP - PAD_BOTTOM;
82	  const xStep = xLabels.length > 1 ? plotW / (xLabels.length - 1) : 0;
83	
84	  const xAt = (i) => PAD_LEFT + i * xStep;
85	  const yAt = (v) => PAD_TOP + plotH * (1 - (v - yMin) / (yMax - yMin));
86	
87	  // Y-axis ticks: choose 4 ticks across the domain
88	  const tickCount = 4;
89	  const ticks = [];
90	  for (let i = 0; i <= tickCount; i += 1) {
91	    const v = yMin + ((yMax - yMin) * i) / tickCount;
92	    ticks.push(v);
93	  }
94	
95	  // Zero baseline (when domain straddles 0)
96	  const zeroLine = yMin < 0 && yMax > 0 ? yAt(0) : null;
97	
98	  const footnote = capFootnote(growthRate);
99	
100	  return (

102	      <div className="chart-title">CAGR glidepath</div>
103	      <div className="chart-legend">
104	        {SCENARIOS.map(({ key, label, color }) => (

107	            {label}
108	          </span>
109	        ))}
110	      </div>

21	function formatPct(value, digits = 1) {
22	  if (value == null || Number.isNaN(value)) return '—';
23	  return `${(value * 100).toFixed(digits)}%`;
24	}

26	function capFootnote(growthRate) {
27	  if (!growthRate || growthRate.cap_applied !== true) return null;
28	  const trailing = growthRate.trailing_3y_cagr;

32	  return `Base-case Y2–Y5 CAGR capped from ${formatPct(trailing)} by ${source} (${formatPct(applied)}).`;
33	}

35	export default function CagrGlidepath({ model }) {
36	  if (!model) return null;
37	  const method = typeof model.method === 'string' ? model.method : '';
38	  if (method.startsWith('pre-profit')) return null;
39	
40	  const fcfTtm = model.fcf_ttm;
41	  const fcfNormalized = model.fcf_normalized;
42	  const scenarios = model.scenarios ?? {};
43	  const growthRate = model.growth_rate ?? {};
44	  const trailing = growthRate.trailing_3y_cagr;
45	  const hasTrailing = trailing != null && Number.isFinite(trailing);
46	
47	  // Y1 anchor: prefer fcf_normalized if positive (handles capex-distorted TTM like AMZN),
48	  // fall back to fcf_ttm if positive, else null → skip Y1 to avoid nonsensical growth rate.
49	  const y1Anchor =
50	    (fcfNormalized != null && Number.isFinite(fcfNormalized) && fcfNormalized > 0)
51	      ? fcfNormalized
52	      : (Number.isFinite(fcfTtm) && fcfTtm > 0)
53	        ? fcfTtm
54	        : null;
55	
56	  // Build series: [trailing?, y1?, y2, y3, y4, y5] per scenario. Drop the
57	  // trailing column entirely when growth_rate.trailing_3y_cagr is missing
58	  // (older pre-v1.11 reports), so we never plot NaN. Drop Y1 when y1Anchor
59	  // is null (negative TTM and no normalised alternative).
60	  const series = SCENARIOS.map(({ key, label, color }) => {
61	    const s = scenarios[key];
62	    if (!s || !Number.isFinite(s.y1_fcf) || !Number.isFinite(s.y2_5_cagr)) {
63	      return null;
64	    }
65	    const y25Cagr = s.y2_5_cagr;
66	    if (y1Anchor !== null) {

68	      const points = hasTrailing
69	        ? [trailing, y1Cagr, y25Cagr, y25Cagr, y25Cagr, y25Cagr]
70	        : [y1Cagr, y25Cagr, y25Cagr, y25Cagr, y25Cagr];
71	      return { key, label, color, points };
72	    }
73	    // Y1 anchor unavailable — skip Y1 point
74	    const points = hasTrailing
75	      ? [trailing, y25Cagr, y25Cagr, y25Cagr, y25Cagr]
76	      : [y25Cagr, y25Cagr, y25Cagr, y25Cagr];
77	    return { key, label, color, points };
78	  }).filter(Boolean);
79	
80	  if (series.length === 0) return null;
81	
82	  const baseLabels = hasTrailing ? X_LABELS : X_LABELS.slice(1);
83	  const xLabels = y1Anchor !== null ? baseLabels : baseLabels.filter((l) => l !== 'Y1');
84	
85	  // Y-axis domain: include trailing + all scenario points, pad 10%
86	  const allValues = series.flatMap((s) => s.points).filter((v) => v != null && Number.isFinite(v));
87	  if (allValues.length === 0) return null;
88	
89	  let yMin = Math.min(0, ...allValues);
90	  let yMax = Math.max(...allValues);
91	  if (yMin === yMax) yMax = yMin + 0.1;
92	  const yPad = (yMax - yMin) * 0.1;
93	  yMin -= yPad;
94	  yMax += yPad;
95	
96	  const plotW = WIDTH - PAD_LEFT - PAD_RIGHT;
97	  const plotH = HEIGHT - PAD_TOP - PAD_BOTTOM;
98	  const xStep = xLabels.length > 1 ? plotW / (xLabels.length - 1) : 0;
99	
100	  const xAt = (i) => PAD_LEFT + i * xStep;
101	  const yAt = (v) => PAD_TOP + plotH * (1 - (v - yMin) / (yMax - yMin));
102	
103	  // Y-axis ticks: choose 4 ticks across the domain
104	  const tickCount = 4;
105	  const ticks = [];
106	  for (let i = 0; i <= tickCount; i += 1) {
107	    const v = yMin + ((yMax - yMin) * i) / tickCount;
108	    ticks.push(v);
109	  }
110	
111	  // Zero baseline (when domain straddles 0)

113

115

> AGENT

ABA-143 is done. The fix in `CagrGlidepath.jsx`:

- Introduces a `y1Anchor` variable that prefers `fcf_normalized` (if positive), falls back to `fcf_ttm` (if positive), and is `null` when both are unavailable/negative
- When `y1Anchor === null` (AMZN case), Y1 is dropped from the series points and the `Y1` label is filtered from the X-axis — connecting trailing 3y directly to Y2
- AMZN now renders with a sensible -15% to 160% Y-axis where Y2–Y5 at 9%/18%/24% is clearly readable and the cap callout fires correctly
- META/NVDA with positive `fcf_ttm` are completely unchanged
